done.title: Your files are ready.
done.closingNote: Closing the window just hides Kensaku, it keeps running in the background. If it seems to disappear, press your shortcut or look in the tray.

scan.onlyFirstTime: Only the first time. After this, every launch is instant.

folders.title: Where do your files live?
folders.lead: Pick the folders to search. You can change this later.
folders.pickMany: pick as many as you like
folders.pathPlaceholder: Or type a path — ~ works, commas separate several
folders.pickerUnavailable: Folder picker unavailable here — type a path below instead. ({{error}})

ocr.title: Read the text in your images
ocr.lead: Screenshots, scans and photos become searchable. Pick an engine.
ocr.tesseractNote: Fast, clean ASCII text; no download needed. Fallback engine.
ocr.ppocrNote: Recommended. ~6 MB, highest recall on dense UI screenshots, fastest batch throughput.
ocr.indraNote: ~27 MB, 80+ languages, rotated/skewed scans; comparable recall, slightly slower.

mode.appLead: Kensaku opens as a normal window, stays in your taskbar, and keeps the index warm while it is open.
mode.launcherLead: Kensaku runs as an ultra-light background daemon. It opens with your shortcut, hides when you click away or press Esc, and stays in the tray.
mode.label: Window mode
mode.appNote: Closing the window quits Kensaku. Reopen it from the taskbar or your app menu.
mode.launcherNote: Closing the window hides it; Kensaku keeps running in the tray. You can switch modes later in Settings.
mode.escHides: Esc hides it again. Kensaku keeps running quietly.
mode.wayland: On Linux with Wayland, bind a system shortcut to kensaku --toggle if the key doesn't register.
mode.closingLauncher: Closing the window just hides Kensaku, it keeps running. If it seems to disappear, press your shortcut or look in the tray.
